issue_context.title: ansible 2.8.6 get_url repeatedly downloads file with force==no
issue_context.body:
##### SUMMARY
Unlike in version 2.8.5, get_url module repeatedly downloads an URL even if destination exists with Ansible 2.8.6

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bug Report

##### COMPONENT NAME
get_url

##### ANSIBLE VERSION
<!--- Paste verbatim output from "ansible --version" between quotes -->
```
$ ansible --version
ansible 2.8.6
  config file = None
  configured module search path = [u'/Users/XXX/.ansible/plugins/modules', u'/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /Users/XXX/.virtualenvs/ansible2.8/lib/python2.7/site-packages/ansible
  executable location = /Users/XXX/.virtualenvs/ansible2.8/bin/ansible
  python version = 2.7.16 (default, Sep  2 2019, 11:59:44) [GCC 4.2.1 Compatible Apple LLVM 10.0.1 (clang-1001.0.46.4)]
```

##### CONFIGURATION
<!--- Paste verbatim output from "ansible-config dump --only-changed" between quotes -->
```
$ ansible-config dump --only-changed
$
```

##### OS / ENVIRONMENT
MacOS


##### STEPS TO REPRODUCE
<!--- Describe exactly how to reproduce the problem, using a minimal test-case -->

<!--- Paste example playbooks or commands between quotes below -->
```yaml
$ touch foofile
$ cat > test_playbook.yaml
---
- hosts: localhost
  connection: local

  tasks:
    - name:           Fetch file
      get_url:
        url:          http://google.com
        dest:         ./foofile
        force:        no

$ ansible-playbook -i 'localhost,' test_playbook.yaml
```

##### EXPECTED RESULTS
No changes, since "foofile" already exists. With the same playbook, a run with Ansible 2.8.5 results in:
```
PLAY RECAP ********************************************************************************************************
localhost                  : ok=2    changed=0    unreachable=0    failed=0    skipped=0    rescued=0    ignored=0
```


##### ACTUAL RESULTS
File gets overwritten/downloaded every time
```
$ ansible-playbook -i 'localhost,' test_playbook.yaml
PLAY [localhost] **************************************************************************************************

TASK [Gathering Facts] ********************************************************************************************
ok: [localhost]

TASK [Fetch file] *************************************************************************************************
changed: [localhost]

PLAY RECAP ********************************************************************************************************
localhost                  : ok=2    changed=1    unreachable=0    failed=0    skipped=0    rescued=0    ignored=0
```

There was a bug in <2.8.6 where we assumed no checksum was a checksum match.  I think we need to further improve the logic to account for this situation too.

Maybe something like:

```diff
diff --git a/lib/ansible/modules/net_tools/basics/get_url.py b/lib/ansible/modules/net_tools/basics/get_url.py
index 3c84cb60e9..3fb72dbe84 100644
--- a/lib/ansible/modules/net_tools/basics/get_url.py
+++ b/lib/ansible/modules/net_tools/basics/get_url.py
@@ -540,7 +540,7 @@ def main():
                 checksum_mismatch = True
 
         # Not forcing redownload, unless checksum does not match
-        if not force and checksum and not checksum_mismatch:
+        if not force and (not checksum or (checksum and not checksum_mismatch)):
             # Not forcing redownload, unless checksum does not match
             # allow file attribute changes
             module.params['path'] = dest
```

More integration tests would need added.

@sivel I tested the proposed patch above and it seems like the logic is fixed and matches the intended behaviour. If the file exists locally, regardless of its contents if skips the download.

What version of ansible do you envision to incorporate the fix in?
@sivel, the condition fix looks good - how soon can it get released? With a large server farm, this bug triggers a stampede effect, where there would be 0 requests normally.

I am not actively working on this issue.  I have provided a proof of concept fix that someone else can validate, make modifications if necessary, provide a pull request to resolve it, and include integration tests.

@gtie @sivel I am currently looking into an implementation of @sivel 's POC and am adding integration tests for this issue too. Currently checking all previous integration tests are not impacted by the change I want to propose.
@hugocartwright, what needs to happen for your PR to get merged? Also, can it get backported to the 2.8 branch?

@hugocartwright, is perhaps the failing test a consequence of changing the test URL from `https://{{ httpbin_host }}/get` to `https://{{ httpbin_host }}/html`? What is the purpose of the URL change so far away from the actual double-download assertion (mid-file vs end-of-file)?

https://github.com/whs-dot-hk/ansible-fedora-desktop/blob/c29a395c5fcd0add23e3189b39eef80fd91aec0d/roles/cuda/tasks/main.yml#L5
/assign @whs-dot-hk

Hi,
Same issue with docker image debian:testing-slim (python2.7) and python:3.7.6-slim-buster.
Works on ansible 2.8.4 and 2.8.5
don't works on 2.8.6 and 2.9.X

This change seems to be the issue
We never get into the conditional block because of the `checksum`
```python
# Not forcing redownload, unless checksum does not match
if not force and checksum and not checksum_mismatch:
    # Not forcing redownload, unless checksum does not match
    # allow file attribute changes
    file_args = module.load_file_common_arguments(module.params, path=dest)
    result['changed'] = module.set_fs_attributes_if_different(file_args, False)
    if result['changed']:
        module.exit_json(msg="file already exists but file attributes changed", **result)
    module.exit_json(msg="file already exists", **result)
```

@sivel I don't see why checksum enters into the desired logic at all.  Even if I did provide a checksum to guard against bad downloads, force:no means I _never_ want to overwrite my existing file.

Documentation of `force` in https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/modules/get_url_module.html#parameter-force says "If no, the file will only be downloaded if the destination does not exist." which is clear, intuitive, and consistent with the meaning of `force` in other contexts -- does the copy module with force:no overwrite an existing file which doesn't match the checksum?  (okay, actually I've never tried that, but I really hope not)

Hi,
I've been watching this issue (and the related PRs like #65340) for a while and I think there is confusion (at least between code and documentation) over what should happen if:
* no `checksum` is given
* `force` is set to `no`
* `dest` exists, but differs from the content at `url`

The documentation for `force` clear says:
> If no, the file will only be downloaded if the destination does not exist.

However, the changes introduced in 2.8.6 (in 7d51cac3301fddf6a876b2f75057f432b0841f04 / #62146) ) change the behaviour to effectively always force a new download - even the commit message for this commit says:
>  Don't treat no checksum as a checksum match

I think we need a clear answer on what should happen in this case (`force: no`, no checksum, file exists but differs) - either:
(a) force a new download and replace the file with contents at URL
(b) keep the file as is

Once we have that answer, fixing the logic should be easy.

Can someone in the right position (module owner?) please pick the desired behaviour?

Cheers,
Vlad

Please fix this - in code or documentation.

(b) is more what i expect reading the documentation
(a) is more an "ansible way" of setting a state ... imho

My workflow as follows:
- download a text file (get_url)
- replace a line (lineinfile)

So this will lead to change twice every time i execute the tasks.
With (b) it would work out of the box
With (a) i need to put in an additional file exists check (what i will do now)
Is anyone making any progress on this? I would love to see this fixed as well, or at least have a work-around.
My (sad) workaround is to do a stat first, and skip the task if the file already exists...

You can work around it with a `when:` like this:
```yaml
- name: Example
  get_url:
    url: https://example.com/file
    dest: /path/to/dest
  when: not '/path/to/dest' is exists # Workaround
```
A more complex example:
```yaml
- name: Example with vars
  get_url:
    url: "{{ item.url }}"
    dest: /path/to/{{ item.dest }}
  when: not ('/path/to/' + item.dest) is exists # Workaround
  with_items:
    - { url: "https://example.com/file1", dest: file1 }
    - { url: "https://example.com/file2", dest: file2 }

```

@gloomytrousers , thanks for the suggestion, but that won't unfortunately work: the `exists` test applies to local files on the Ansible *controller* machine, not the target host.  To check for presence on the target host, an explicit `stat` task is required...
@vladimir-mencl-eresearch thanks for the info - we learn something new every day :-) Yes, in my case I'm running the playbook against the local machine so this works for me.

I am seeing this too, and it is difficult because I have some code that runs (depending on the situation) sometimes with 'net access, and sometimes without.

So when the web proxy is down, the code fails because it is trying to download something that is already there (and we are upgrading from pre-2.8.5 to 2.9.x and running into this)

I am going to wrap a complicated check around to make the `when:` reliable, but it would be nice to make this work!

Thanks!
I am currently using @vladimir-mencl-eresearch 's workaround using `stat` but am still curious about a permanent fix. Is anyone working on it? If not, why not? Can I help?

Let's recap, shall we?

This issue has been opened for a little while and seems to have fallen into a crack with #64626 waiting for contributor feedback and #65340 falsely considering the issue fixed (it's true that the task correctly registers as "not changed", but `fetch_url()` is still called).

It seems to me that, as @vladimir-mencl-eresearch correctly mentions, the heart of the matter is that behavior began diverging from documentation with #62146 which fixed another problem. It's possible that #62146 is the correct behavior, but in that case, it should be accompanied by a documentation update. Decision needed.

To ease the decision, I've submitted a new PR which applied cleanly to the devel branch that essentially reverts #62146 and adjusts tests accordingly.

Hey, so I've just found this issue, after being confused too… @hsoft - yeah, what you wrote and your PR at #79518 makes sense to me.

But I started digging into the original PR at #62146 (pinging the author: @sivel) and the corresponding issue #61978 to see why that change has been made, and I think I understand the whole problem now. The problem is that "force" across this module kind of means two different things:

1. Whether it should force the download if file exists
2. How it should set cache headers for the download, and if it should force the download ignoring the cache (instead of allowing the download to return 304)

@sivel probably understood "force" as only 2), and expected the command to always try to perform the download if force == false, with force == true only changing that it forces the file contents to actually be downloaded instead of allowing 304. We apparently understand "force" as 1). The question is which of those should it mean (it seems to me that docs currently imply 1), and if we perhaps need another option to differentiate between these two?

If "force" means only 2, there is no way to completely skip any other checks if *some* file exists at that path as we expected, other than adding additional workarounds. If "force" means only 1, then there is no way to always make a request to check for a newer version of the file allowing a 304 response.
Any update on this ? It was created 4 years ago. We are waiting since 2022(!) for a decision (!) if either the code or the doc needs to be updated.

Please make a decision about the intended behaviour of the force parameter and/or whether to add a new parameter to support both the "update file if changed" and "only download if not existant" use cases, so that someone can create a PR for this.

I keep stumbling over this issue and until just now I thought it's an issue with check mode (see https://github.com/ansible/ansible/issues/65687), but no, the module actually doesn't work in the documented way.

Just wasted a lot of time diagnosing this 5-year-old issue. Notwithstanding the documented behaviour is very odd; that is, whether or not it overwrites the destination is supposed to depend on whether or not the destination is a directory or file, it does not even behave in accordance with the documentation. That is, it always overwrites the destination file, if it has changed from the source URL (regardless of `force` being `false` and regardless of the destination being a file). Either the documentation needs correcting or the software does.

In any case, we need a way to opt into only downloading the file once, when we do not wish to keep downloading it when it already exists.

Following is my specific use-case:

```yaml
- name: Download Coolify sources
  get_url:
    url: '{{ item.url|default(item) }}'
    dest: /data/coolify/source/{{ item.name if item is mapping else item|basename }}
    owner: 9999
    mode: 0700
  loop:
    - https://cdn.coollabs.io/coolify/docker-compose.yml
    - https://cdn.coollabs.io/coolify/docker-compose.prod.yml
    - url: https://cdn.coollabs.io/coolify/.env.production
      name: .env
    - https://cdn.coollabs.io/coolify/upgrade.sh
```

Any changes subsequently made to `.env` will be overwritten by `get_url` with the original from the CDN.

For the record,  this behavior is easy to circumvent with a presence test on the local file first.
But **only after** you have some understanding of the `force` parameter behavior and the incomplete documentation.
So losing much time having to debug get_url beforehand.

````
- stat:
    path: /my/dest/file
    get_checksum: no
  register: task_geturl_file
  changed_when: task_geturl_file.stat.exists == false

- get_url:
    dest: /my/dest/file
    ...
  when: task_geturl_file is changed
````

> For the record, this behavior is easy to circumvent

Not so easy when you're looping, is it.

You're right, as this requires a good knowledge of ansible to handle this situation.  
Having get_url working as expected/desired would be much simpler.

If you don't already have something for this, there are currently 2 working options : 

Option 1 :
The least cumbersome, but still more than a single loop on a get_url task : looping over an include_tasks. 
The generated "item" variable from the loop is usable in the included task file, so it is possible to do a stat + get_url on a single file. This will make the code much easier to read.

```
# main task file 
- include_tasks: get_url_with_presence_test.yml
  with_items:
    - "url1"
    - "url2"
    ...
  # rename the generated item to something else to prevent any conflict
  loop_control:
    loop_var: urlItem
```

```
---
# dedicated file : get_url_with_presence_test.yml

- name: "Presence check of {{ urlItem |basename }}"
  stat:
    path: "/my/dest/{{ urlItem |basename }}"
    get_checksum: no
  register: task_geturl_file
  changed_when: task_geturl_file.stat.exists == false

- name: "Retrieving the file {{ urlItem |basename }}"
  get_url:
    url: "{{ urlItem }}"
    dest: "/my/dest/{{ urlItem |basename }}"
      ...
  when: task_geturl_file is changed
```

The downside is on the log output when executed, it will add 2 tasks per url instead of a single one for the whole list.

---

Option 2 :
Not really desired, but can be useful to know this is possible for special cases :
the registered variable from the output of a loop will have its data under a `.result[ ]` array.
But all the items listed in a loop will keep the same order in the result array : the first item listed in the task will be at index 0, the second at index 1, and so on, item n will be at index n-1.
With this, the desired element can be selected without error from the registered variable output. 
```
- stat:
    path: "/my/dest/{{ item |basename }}"
    get_checksum: no
  with_items
    - "url1"
    - "url2"
    ...
  register: task_geturl_file
  # this should work even if in a the loop
  changed_when: task_geturl_file.stat.exists == false

- get_url:
    path: "/my/dest/{{ item.url |basename }}"
    ...
  with_items
    - { url: "url1", when: "{{ task_geturl_file.results.0.stat.exists == false }}" }
    - { url: "url2", when: "{{ task_geturl_file.results.1.stat.exists == false }}" }
    - { url: "url3", when: "{{ task_geturl_file.results.2.stat.exists == false }}" }
    ..
  when: item.when |bool
```
It is something I'm using in some rare cases. 
But it gives me a headache each time I need to change something in it.
